title: Web servers: Nginx, Apache and Caddy

videos.script: Type an address, press enter, and a page appears. Something on the other end read your request and decided what to send back. {{request}} That something is a web server. It listens on a port. It reads a request. And it answers in one of three ways: with a file, with an answer it asked an application for, or with an answer of its own. {{three}} This course is about doing those three things well. The first half puts an application online, behind a server, with a certificate and sensible defences. The second half makes it answer fast, by not doing the same work twice. {{halves}} It starts here, with a machine of your own. You build an Ubuntu server on your computer, and install a small bookshop on it. {{lab}} Then you meet the three servers you will find most often. Nginx, Apache and Caddy. Each one serves the same files, and each one does it a little differently. {{servers}} And you break one on purpose, to learn the habit that keeps a site up while you change it. {{break}}
